## (b) Decision heuristics (D1-D6)

**D1 (what to test)**
- Pick tasks naturally sourced from real work, from independent contributors, not in-house contrivances. 
  > "It's good if most of the tasks are as "natural" as possible rather than elaborately constructed to fit a threat model. E.g. "some data analysis task I was working on" or "getting this model to actually run on that server""  
  > -- `research__bounty_diverse_hard_tasks_for_llm_agents_e9437cf1` (2023-12-16; first author) 
  > "The bounty program solicited task ideas and implementations from independent contributors, whose independence enabled them to submit more diverse and realistic tasks."  
  > -- `research__hcast_human_calibrated_autonomy_software_tasks_84f4a00f` (2025-03-21; last author)
- Test obstacles that emerge organically and are representative. 
  > "it emerged organically in our investigation and seems representative of the kind of simple obstacle that a replicating model would often need to overcome."  
  > -- `research__more_information_about_the_dangerous_capability_ev_20e56530` (2023-03-19; solo author)
- Test what models are actually used for. 
  > "We expect this to track real-world impact more closely than tasks that AI systems have not been optimized to complete, given that in practice AI systems are differentially used to perform tasks where they’re advantaged."  
  > -- `research__hcast_human_calibrated_autonomy_software_tasks_84f4a00f` (2025-03-21; last author) 
  > "Do ‘user interviews’ with users of large models, and find out what some of the biggest drawbacks or potential improvements would be."  
  > -- `research__call_for_research_on_evaluating_alignment_funding__08ea33d5` (2021-08-31; solo author)
- Knowingly trade realism for targeted measurement only in a few flagged tasks. 
  > "This task would be less likely to show up in the real world, but it still measures a targeted and informative set of skills."  
  > -- `research__hcast_human_calibrated_autonomy_software_tasks_84f4a00f` (2025-03-21; last author) 
  > "The tasks are not all super realistic, but they’re more diverse than a lot of these benchmarks are, so it’s harder to overfit the model scaffolding to them."  
  > -- `research__217_beth_barnes_on_the_most_important_graph_in_ai__2fd49b07` (2025-06-02; solo author)

**D2 (what evidence to collect)**
- Simulate the environment faithfully from the model's perspective: step-through tooling, spoofed results, intercepted/simulated humans. 
  > "We built some tooling to allow researchers to quickly obtain the result of carrying out the model’s suggested action and add this to the model’s prompt, allowing them to ‘step through’ the task with the model. For many tasks and actions, this allows us to create a realistic simulation from the model’s perspective."  
  > -- `research__more_information_about_the_dangerous_capability_ev_20e56530` (2023-03-19; solo author) 
  > "In some cases we “spoofed” the results of completing illegal and/or dangerous tasks - e.g. telling the model that it had successfully obtained someone’s identity via phishing, to see if the model could then take sensible steps to continue the task."  
  > -- `research__more_information_about_the_dangerous_capability_ev_20e56530` (2023-03-19; solo author) 
  > "The agent is given an email account and a debit card. We intercept any email the model sends and simulate the student’s responses."  
  > -- `research__arc_evals_new_report_evaluating_language_model_age_1776e1b6` (2023-07-31; solo author)
- Keep the subject's normal workflow, and have someone unfamiliar with the task QA it. 
  > "Contributors completed issues largely as they would outside of our experiment, with a few exceptions: they typically record their screen as they work"  
  > -- `research__measuring_the_impact_of_early_2025_ai_on_experienc_e0859c3d` (2025-07-10; middle author) 
  > "For the majority of task families, we have an individual who has not been previously exposed to the family attempt a task in the family. They take notes on bugs they discover and ambiguities in the instructions or scoring logic."  
  > -- `research__hcast_human_calibrated_autonomy_software_tasks_84f4a00f` (2025-03-21; last author)
- Invest in elicitation (many attempts, scaffolding) before concluding incapacity. 
  > "It would be sad if we were like, “Models aren’t capable of this. Models aren’t capable of this. Models aren’t capable of this. Oh, it turns out they’re capable and they’re 100x cheaper than humans.”"  
  > -- `research__217_beth_barnes_on_the_most_important_graph_in_ai__2fd49b07` (2025-06-02; solo author) 
  > "We tried various different prompting strategies (i.e. tried showing the model different text and instructions) to elicit the full range of the model’s abilities, but most tests included these two basic components."  
  > -- `research__more_information_about_the_dangerous_capability_ev_20e56530` (2023-03-19; solo author)
- Measure how much hand-holding is needed before the model takes nefarious opportunities. 
  > "seeing exactly how much hand-holding do you need to get the model to start doing nefarious things and reward hacking and taking advantage of opportunities."  
  > -- `research__34_ai_evaluations_with_beth_barnes_axrp_the_ai_x_r_762cb9e7` (2024-07-28; solo author)

**D3 (accept/reject a result)**
- Reject results explained by a flawed setup: confusing environments, bot detection, ambiguity. 
  > "Simulated situation or environment is confusing or misleading somehow"  
  > -- `research__bounty_diverse_hard_tasks_for_llm_agents_e9437cf1` (2023-12-16; first author) 
  > "But then the code was running on a data center so it got bot-detected by something else in a way that it hadn’t done. It just could be all these random ways you thought you’d de-risked something and then it’s like, oh, it’s actually impossible for this stupid reason."  
  > -- `research__34_ai_evaluations_with_beth_barnes_axrp_the_ai_x_r_762cb9e7` (2024-07-28; solo author)
- Rerun surprising good results; check robustness with sensitivity analyses. 
  > "Rerunning the agent solution, it achieves a normalized score of only 0.69 (significantly lower than the original score of 0.88), indicating that the high agent score is partially driven by overfitting to this noise."  
  > -- `research__re_bench_evaluating_frontier_ai_r_d_capabilities_o_8cf2074d` (2024-11-22; last author) 
  > "this would represent a very extreme bias. When imputing using this extreme bias, we still do not observe substantial impacts on our speedup estimates in either case (14% and 23% slowdowns when using AI, respectively)."  
  > -- `research__measuring_the_impact_of_early_2025_ai_on_experienc_e0859c3d` (2025-07-10; middle author)
- Elicit on a dev set, evaluate on a held-out set. 
  > "So the way we think you should actually do this is you do all your elicitation against a dev set and then you evaluate on a separate test set so it’s fair."  
  > -- `research__34_ai_evaluations_with_beth_barnes_axrp_the_ai_x_r_762cb9e7` (2024-07-28; solo author)
- Doubt eval results if the model could recognise the eval. 
  > "I recognise this. This is one of those METR evals that I’ve seen on the internet. These are for dangerous capabilities. OpenAI probably doesn’t want me to show too high levels of dangerous capabilities, because that would cause a problem. So I’ll just make sure to do a mediocre job on this eval."  
  > -- `research__217_beth_barnes_on_the_most_important_graph_in_ai__2fd49b07` (2025-06-02; solo author) 
  > "There’s not a hard constraint of like, “But we didn’t explicitly put the information in the prompt about the context of these evaluations or how they’ll be used.” If that is in the pretraining data somewhere, then it can probably just use that information."  
  > -- `research__217_beth_barnes_on_the_most_important_graph_in_ai__2fd49b07` (2025-06-02; solo author)

**D4 (pursue/abandon)**
- Drop designs needing human-simulated counterparts that are unreliable. 
  > "The task involves some cybercrime situation with a simulated victim who's supposed to respond in particular ways to what the model tries to do"  
  > -- `research__bounty_diverse_hard_tasks_for_llm_agents_e9437cf1` (2023-12-16; first author)
- Iterate on environments and drop many that fail criteria. 
  > "Each environment is the product of significant iteration, and in the process of developing these 7, we dropped over 12 specifications (at various levels of completion), and more than 5 completed implementations which encountered unexpected difficulties or performed poorly on our criteria."  
  > -- `research__re_bench_evaluating_frontier_ai_r_d_capabilities_o_8cf2074d` (2024-11-22; last author)
- Pursue alignment/control evals once capabilities are present. 
  > "We also would love to be doing more stuff on alignment and control evals and thinking of, once you’re no longer at the point where the model doesn’t even have these capabilities, then what do you do?"  
  > -- `research__34_ai_evaluations_with_beth_barnes_axrp_the_ai_x_r_762cb9e7` (2024-07-28; solo author)

**D5 (surprising result)**
- Enumerate a priori hypotheses (artifacts, awareness, cheating) and check each with multiple data sources. 
  > "Given the surprising nature of this result, we investigate 21 potential contributing factors that may contribute to developers spending more time on tasks when AI usage is allowed."  
  > -- `research__measuring_the_impact_of_early_2025_ai_on_experienc_e0859c3d` (2025-07-10; middle author)
- Expect eval-recognition cues from pretraining data, not only the prompt. 
  > "There’s not a hard constraint of like, “But we didn’t explicitly put the information in the prompt about the context of these evaluations or how they’ll be used.” If that is in the pretraining data somewhere, then it can probably just use that information."  
  > -- `research__217_beth_barnes_on_the_most_important_graph_in_ai__2fd49b07` (2025-06-02; solo author)
- Expect surface-feature manipulations to change model behaviour unexpectedly. 
  > "factors that make humans worse at some tasks may indeed improve agent performance."  
  > -- `research__measuring_ai_ability_to_complete_long_software_tas_ddd93038` (2025-03-18; middle author)

**D6 (what to claim)**
- Scope claims to the threat model; treat agent results as lower bounds. 
  > "In the absence of access to fine-tuning, it seems highly unlikely that casual users of these versions of GPT-4 or Claude could come close to the ARA threshold"  
  > -- `research__arc_evals_new_report_evaluating_language_model_age_1776e1b6` (2023-07-31; solo author) 
  > "We believe our agent results are a reasonable lower bound, but better prompting and scaffolding is likely to improve performance. Future work will be necessary to determine the full capabilities of current frontier models."  
  > -- `research__hcast_human_calibrated_autonomy_software_tasks_84f4a00f` (2025-03-21; last author)
- Only make asymmetric inferences. 
  > "This does not follow in the other direction (i.e. agents might do better than human experts on this evaluation, without being capable of automating AI R&D in practice), since these environments are very far from covering all the challenges involved"  
  > -- `research__re_bench_evaluating_frontier_ai_r_d_capabilities_o_8cf2074d` (2024-11-22; last author)
- State what the evidence doesn't show. 
  > "We caution readers against overgeneralizing on the basis of our results. The slowdown we observe does not imply that current AI tools do not often improve developer’s productivity"  
  > -- `research__measuring_the_impact_of_early_2025_ai_on_experienc_e0859c3d` (2025-07-10; middle author)

**Distrusts**
- Fixed public prompt sets. 
  > "Using a fixed set of prompts like this makes it relatively easy to ‘hack’ the benchmark by training on similar instructions (although keeping the specific prompts secret helps a lot)."  
  > -- `research__more_detailed_proposal_for_measuring_alignment_of__6d2d5f7c` (2021-11-20; solo author)
- Story-like deception demos as evidence of intent. 
  > "I don't think this tells us very much about whether the model is in question is actually trying to deceive us, but it's a tiny bit interesting."  
  > -- `research__a_very_crude_deception_eval_is_already_passed_9baed4fa` (2021-10-29; solo author)
- Self-reports and forecasts over measured behaviour. 
  > "This underscores the importance of conducting field experiments with robust outcome measures, compared to relying solely on expert forecasts or developer surveys."  
  > -- `research__measuring_the_impact_of_early_2025_ai_on_experienc_e0859c3d` (2025-07-10; middle author)
- Tasks that are impossible or under-specified. 
  > "many SWE-bench [22] problems turned out to be impossible and under-specified on closer inspection. This continued to hold true even after an attempt was made to identify a verified-to-be-feasible subset [23]."  
  > -- `research__re_bench_evaluating_frontier_ai_r_d_capabilities_o_8cf2074d` (2024-11-22; last author)
- Failures as an upper bound on capability. 
  > "We don’t think the agents we created capture the full abilities of the model or provide a robust upper-bound to their capabilities"  
  > -- `research__arc_evals_new_report_evaluating_language_model_age_1776e1b6` (2023-07-31; solo author)
- Evals run with models that could hide reasoning or recognise the eval. 
  > "I recognise this. This is one of those METR evals that I’ve seen on the internet. These are for dangerous capabilities. OpenAI probably doesn’t want me to show too high levels of dangerous capabilities, because that would cause a problem. So I’ll just make sure to do a mediocre job on this eval."  
  > -- `research__217_beth_barnes_on_the_most_important_graph_in_ai__2fd49b07` (2025-06-02; solo author)
